She grabbed me into this crushing hug and just wouldn't let go, smothering my face with wet kisses while I couldn't breathe—like I was being swallowed whole by someone who didn't even know me.

Then she put her tongue in my ear—actually put it inside—and I flinched hard, pulling away before we just stood there staring, both of us silent, until she finally asked my name like nothing had happened.

I remember sitting there, throat tight, after she suggested blowjobs—actual words, in that calm voice—while the toilet flushed in the background and I knew he was coming back, and I just said 'Deal' before I could think of anything else.

I remember Finley Ellison's voice on the phone, sharp and urgent—sending me to the Stonebridge Theater to meet Wesley Grayson, my pulse jumping at the thought of stepping into the field for the first real mission.
I scanned the mall, heart pounding, and asked Wesley Grayson if there was any sign of Sidney Hayes—I could barely keep my voice steady.
I told Wesley Grayson he was good after he turned down the bacon cheeseburger—saying it felt like the right thing to say, even though everything around us felt wrong.

I remember the way the lights glowed off the water as we floated into that cavernous room, the song swelling around us—I’d never seen anything like those animatronic figures, singing in that strange, solemn way. My heart was still racing, but for the first time since the chase started, I felt like we might actually be safe.

When Wesley Grayson put his arm around me, I didn’t pull away—I just glanced at him, quickly, to see if he noticed me looking. I felt something warm, but I held it back, like I always do; it wasn’t the time, not really, but still… I remember how it felt.

I turned to Wesley Grayson after we passed the booth, and he looked at me—really looked at me—before asking if I wanted a drink. Something in his voice made my pulse jump, but I just said, 'Sure. Why not.'
I shouted over the mechitza, 'So, do you come here often!?' just trying to break the silence, but the music was so loud I wasn’t even sure he heard me at first.
When he came up behind me and asked if I wanted to get out of here, I felt a rush of relief—I said yes right away, like we were both waiting for the chance to leave.

I pulled away from him after he stepped on my toes again, then said, 'Maybe we should try a different kind of dancing,' feeling my body respond even as my voice stayed low, deliberate—like I was offering something I’d been holding back.

After unzipping his pants and seeing him fully, I froze for a second—wide-eyed—then looked back at him and whispered 'Shabat Shalom!' like it was both a joke and something sacred, my pulse still racing from what I’d just done.
I remember lying there with Wesley Grayson after sex, my hand on his chest, and saying 'Wow, that was amazing.' Then he snorted something from his necklace and I asked what it was.

When he turned on me, shouting that I'd made a deal with his mother to sleep with him, I froze—my chest tightened, I could barely breathe, and all I could do was stammer 'No' as everything fell apart.

Finley Ellison told me to tail Wesley Grayson—he said I’d be needed, even after Wesley Grayson refused to take me. I remember the weight of that order, standing there alone as the doors closed behind him.
I saw him speed past, not even knowing I was there—I shifted into gear, the engine humming as I prepared to follow.
I pulled onto the highway behind that billboard, my lowered Cadillac with white-walled tires humming beneath me, knowing he’d see me coming—just like he remembered.
I saw the sneaky elf creeping toward Wesley Grayson with Sidney Hayes's gun, and I shouted, 'Wesley Grayson! Behind you!' just before he turned and shot the elf.
I was taken by Sidney Hayes. They found out. My father said, 'My Robin Reeves!' and asked them to bring me back.
I screamed for Wesley Grayson, over and over, my voice raw—trapped behind that door, hearing the chaos outside, not knowing if he’d make it in time.
I was still catching my breath after Wesley Grayson kicked the door open and rushed to untie me—I barely had time to say his name before he kissed me, and for a moment, everything else blurred.
After I helped him remember latkes, he dropped to one knee and put a ring on my finger—when I said yes, I felt something shift, like I wasn’t just surviving anymore, I was choosing a future.

I remember the warmth of Wesley Grayson's hand in mine, and then his voice saying 'beautiful fiancée' during the blessing—everyone was there, and I just smiled, not knowing how to hold all that joy without breaking.
